🪔 In a city famous for wood carving, one temple was carved entirely from stone.

This is Patan Durbar Square, just across the river from Kathmandu. The tall stone shikhara is the Krishna Mandir, built by the Malla kings — and around it stand palace courtyards, pagoda temples and some of the finest Newar craftsmanship in Nepal. The square is part of the Kathmandu Valley UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Come in the early morning, when the square is quiet and the first devotees arrive with offerings.

🙏 Our 3-day Kathmandu Heritage & Culture tour covers Patan, Kathmandu and Bhaktapur Durbar Squares, Pashupatinath, Boudhanath and Swayambhunath — with a private guide and every entry fee included.

Stone, wood or brass — which craft would you stop to watch? 👇

The jewel-blue lake in this photo is Phoksundo (3,611 m) — and it's only the beginning of Upper Dolpo. 💙

This is one of Nepal's most remote treks, on the Tibet border, where the ancient Bon religion still lives beside Tibetan Buddhism. Before you dream too far, the honest facts:

✈️ There is no road in — you fly Kathmandu to Nepalgunj, then a mountain flight to Juphal
⛺ It's a full camping trek, with tents, a cook and kitchen staff
⛰️ You cross Kang La (5,151 m) to Shey Gompa, the Crystal Mountain, and later Jeng La (5,090 m)
🗓️ 26 days, rated Very Challenging — acclimatisation days are built in

We run it privately for your group, full board in camp, with every permit arranged.
